## Forms · Submit ID Setup → `n8n_submitIdSetup(actor, data, include)`
Runs the **real** `submitEmployeeIDSetup`: writes *ID Setup Results*, advances the workflow, sends the HR Verification email.

**Required** (FormContracts r2 `id_setup`, verified): `workflowId siteDocsWorkerId siteDocsJobCode dssUsername dssPassword`
`siteDocsJobCode` ∈ `Hourly 1 | Hourly 2 | Salary 1 | Salary 2 | Supervisor | Manager` (hard-coded options, **not** George's SiteDocs title codes HRLY-U/Site-Sup — map them first).
**Optional:** `siteDocsUsername siteDocsPassword` (UI requires them only when the request's Systems contains "SiteDocs") `setupNotes bossWisCreated(Yes|No) siteDocsBadgeCreated(Yes|No)`; via `extra`: `formId` (ignored — regenerated).
**Omit `internalEmployeeId`** — the id minted at Create Initial Request is used automatically. A different value is honoured only when the *real session principal* (efx-bot) is in `CONFIG.ADMIN_EMAILS`; otherwise `E_UPSTREAM` "pre-assigned … cannot be changed". There is no override flag.
Every submit **appends** a row (no update-in-place) → step "HR Verification Needed"; Hourly + no system access also emails credentials and creates the Safety item.

Heads-up: `dssPassword` is stored by Forms exactly as the UI does today, and it will also sit in this workflow's execution data. Consider *Settings → Save execution data* on the calling workflow.

### Attribution
Pass `actor` from the calling workflow so Forms records who did it, e.g.
`{{ { id: 'n8n:' + $workflow.name, email: 'efx-bot@team-group.com', display: $workflow.name + ' (n8n)' } }}`
If omitted the Router attributes the call to itself. `idempotencyKey` (optional) makes a retry replay the first result for 10 min.
Errors throw as `EFX <CODE>: message` — attach an error output or error workflow on the calling node.
